input.query: Do the authors offer a hypothesis for why Twitter data makes better predictions about the inventory of languages used in each country?

output.reason: The evidence supports an answer. The paper notes Twitter data makes better predictions about the language inventory (abstract) and that Twitter has fewer missing languages than web-crawled data. The Discussion offers hypotheses for why Twitter and web data diverge: Twitter matches populations better when weighted by GDP and worse by internet-usage statistics, implying Twitter represents wealthier populations; an alternate interpretation is that the collection is based on urban areas, which tend to be wealthier. Additionally, the false-positive discussion notes English and Spanish are very common on Twitter, so countries using these languages are well represented by default. These constitute the authors' hypotheses/explanations.

claims.text: The paper reports that Twitter data makes better predictions about the inventory of languages used in each country.

The authors state that given available ground-truth language-use data, Twitter has fewer missing languages than the web-crawled corpus in countries where not all census languages are found in digital texts.

The authors note that English and Spanish are very common on Twitter, so any country predominantly using these two languages will have a good representation by default; this is presented as a factor disguising results rather than as a hypothesis for Twitter's overall advantage.

The authors hypothesize that Twitter matches populations better when weighted by GDP and worse by internet-usage statistics, implying Twitter represents more wealthy populations than web-crawled data, with an alternate interpretation that the collection is based on urban areas. This hypothesis concerns population representation, not the language inventory result.
The authors state that more research is needed to distinguish between immigration, tourism, and business as sources of false-positive languages in digital datasets.
